rows.title: NFL wind: four Sunday totals to verify
rows.observation: The November 1 source selections are NE–MIA under 43.5 (-113), LAC–LAR under 45.5 (-111), ATL–TB under 43.5 (-111), and IND–JAX under 46.5 (-110). The screen uses average wind of at least 10 mph and temperatures from 33 to 90 degrees; displayed history is 635-467-10 with 11% ROI.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: these are source claims, not verified game-time weather effects. Stadium shelter and roof conditions can invalidate an outdoor weather proxy. Historical ROI is not a forecast for these four games.
rows.next_check: Verify venue, roof/open-air exposure and forecast near kickoff; compare the exact current total and price. Re-capture tomorrow before a new decision. No automatic wind adjustment.

rows.title: Portland–Utah: investigate the under
rows.observation: Action lists Under 232.5 at -112 as a system selection for October 31. Its displayed history is 534 wins, 434 losses, 9 pushes and 7% ROI. Filters include division games in the regular season, under support at 40% or less, and a total falling by at least one point from open to close.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: closing-line information is unavailable when an earlier ticket is placed. This is a third-party historical screen, not our calibrated win probability. The discovery row and expanded chart also disagree on total units; those units are not used.
rows.next_check: Compare the same sportsbook total at the actual decision time, verify line movement and current injuries/pace, then track an independent forward benchmark. Do not apply a fixed probability boost or copy the source stake.

rows.title: System discovery: win rate alone can mislead
rows.observation: The catalog includes both winning and losing historical screens. Its college-football Sharp Money screen shows 51% wins and -1% ROI; an MLB public-fade moneyline screen shows 59% wins and -3% ROI.
rows.interpretation: Use price-adjusted returns, sample size and forward results; neither a sharp-money label nor a high hit rate proves value. Selecting only the best historical screens risks selection bias.
rows.next_check: Keep source systems separate from agency results; test rules prospectively with timestamped inputs and realistic prices before changing betting behavior.

rows.title: College football: compare external model disagreements
rows.observation: At capture the dashboard displayed South Alabama +6.5 versus projection +2, Air Force +0.5 versus -3.5, and Kansas State +2.5 versus -1.2 for October 31 matchups. These are external model comparison leads, not accepted picks or verified book offers.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: a forecast disagreement identifies something to investigate. It does not establish which model is right. The dashboard supplies no named executable sportsbook for these displayed offers.
rows.next_check: Resolve full team/event identities and current sportsbook contracts, compare our forecast and injuries, and preserve the disagreement for later outcome scoring.

cfbd.note: Equal-game averages of prior-week CFBD PPA/play; offense higher / defense allowed lower. Independent provider cross-check, correlated with EPA, not an extra probability boost. Missing games remain unknown; season aggregate is not used for historical cutoffs.

used.reason: Wisconsin Badgers offense -0.009 (8 games) vs Maryland Terrapins defense allowed +0.189 (8 games); Maryland Terrapins offense +0.053 (8 games) vs Wisconsin Badgers defense allowed +0.026 (8 games); CFBD PPA Wisconsin Badgers: offense +0.083 (8 games), defense allowed -0.026 (8 games); CFBD PPA Maryland Terrapins: offense +0.031 (8 games), defense allowed +0.180 (8 games). Offensive EPA: higher is better. Defensive EPA allowed: lower is better; negative is favorable. These are equal-game averages of non-garbage-time EPA/play, not opponent-adjusted ratings. The existing CFB spread forecast already uses opponent-adjusted EPA alongside other metrics; do not add these descriptive averages to its probability again. Passing/rushing are context, not a separately validated matchup edge. Missing values mean unknown. evidence_decisions.note: New paper evaluations use supported fresh evidence. CFBD quality-screen v1 is active for CFB moneylines and laying-points spreads: a joint offensive/defensive disadvantage with four-game samples raises required edge by 2 percentage points and caps stakes at one unit. It can change takes to passes without changing forecast probabilities. Totals and underdog spreads retain existing rules. Experimental, not proven profitable. Injury scenarios can change NBA prop forecasts (maximum 5 percentage points; half-unit stake cap). Falling minutes and matched moneyline crowding can raise required edge. Verified AI caution/reject assessments can tighten or hold a decision; narrative summaries cannot set probabilities. These hypotheses are not proven profitable. Counterpoint keeps its separate inverse experiment; NFL prop holds remain.
limitations: No unattended Action Network collection; snapshots expire after 30 minutes
Spread/total splits need exact source-line identity and remain display-only
Missing evidence retains the original forecast and is explicitly recorded
Existing tickets are never reselected or rewritten

decision_policy.note: Active experimental paper rule: for moneylines and spreads laying points (including pick-em), if the selected team has at least 0.05 lower offensive PPA/play AND at least 0.05 higher defensive PPA allowed than its opponent, require 2 additional percentage points of model edge and cap the stake at one unit. All four overall samples need at least four games and fresh, matched CFBD evidence. Totals, underdog spreads, missing/stale samples and mixed evidence retain existing rules. This is an unvalidated selection screen, not a calibrated probability model. Counterpoint keeps its inverse experiment.

claude_reviews.summary: Top observations (hypotheses/missing validation unless noted): (1) prop_research.py:147-150 refreshes the reference quote only from fresh_quotes and does not reject quotes observed at or after tip; with tip<=now rows moving straight to settlement, in-play or post-tip observations could be stored as the reference. It is labelled verified_closing_line=False, but verify props.fresh_quotes enforces pre-tip. (2) prop_research.py:126-131: the specialist forecast selects the contract by maximum edge across sides/books (max over options at line 129), then owner and consensus are scored on that same selected contract. The selection is conditioned on the minutes_usage model's own edge, so its Brier/log-loss/unit_return is optimistically biased relative to the benchmarks scored on its picks (selection effect, not leakage). Also line 136 marks owner_p/market_p as SHADOW_CANDIDATE at gap>=.02 with no calibration check, and the market consensus never uses the quote's own book prices, so gaps vs. the same price can be inconsistent. (3) bankroll_policy.py:48-62 uses base=min(initial,equity) but open_limit/risk accounting treats opposing tickets at full stake (intended, conservative). The per-sport reserve at line 52-54 applies only to the sportsbook regime for NBA/NFL game lines; the 'beyond_24h' room applies only when the new game is distant (line 50), while missing tip_utc on existing tickets counts as distant, which can silently starve long-dated allowance. Also prop_research.py:120 compares latest-appearance team_id to the snapshot team, and prop_research.py:118 assigns agents by player-id hash modulo a changing agent list, so identity can drift across runs (hypothesis). Tests are synthetic and do not certify model quality.

1) news_hypotheses.py:24-36/62-69 and context_trends.py:63-70: failure handling is fragile. In news_hypotheses.tick, if history_source or injuries load fails, `source`/`meta` are unbound, but the exception path only sets history=None, so later use is guarded only by that flag; however an exception type outside (OSError,ValueError,KeyError) (e.g., pandas ParserError/EmptyDataError, AttributeError on missing columns like fetched_utc/nba_team_id) will crash the whole tick before the transaction. Hypothesis, not definite bug. 2) Temporal/identity concerns: news_hypotheses.py:84/98 identity digest includes source sha256 and history sha256, so every new injury snapshot or history refresh creates a fresh hypothesis for the same game/player/stat, contradicting the comment at line 97 ('one predeclared hypothesis per player/stat/game') and enabling post-hoc cherry-picking and duplicate settled rows inflating Brier/unit stats in public() (lines 139-150). Likely definite design defect. Also line 93-95 compares nba_player_id/nba_team_id strings to pid/team without normalization; a dtype/format mismatch silently yields 'No confirmed-out teammate'. 3) Calibration/model quality: hypothesis() line 54 shrinks the without-teammate mean toward baseline but the baseline already uses last-30 games (which may include the absence), and line 56 scales mean linearly with minutes; edge>=.02 threshold at line 117 is uncalibrated, 'SHADOW_CANDIDATE' unit returns (line 147) are selected on the same quote (best-edge option, line 110) so are optimistically biased; no multiple-comparison control. context_trends line 85 picks min(book) alphabetically rather than best price, and context() lines 26-38 treat a quote observed up to 90 minutes pre-tip as the line (not closing), though it is disclosed. Tests are for a different snapshot, so nothing here is certified.

Top observations (hypotheses/missing validation unless noted; I did not run code). (1) sportsbook.py:189-201 vs 194-205: selection and the stake use pre-cap values while evidence-adjusted probability/edge is reused; edge for stake sizing at line 201 is computed from the evidence-adjusted probability but memory_details (line 212) records p (adjusted) as 'adjusted_probability' with the base in 'baseline'; the selection key max(x[0]-threshold) is fine, but 'edge' passed to stake is the adjusted edge, so a probability blend from evidence_decisions.py:134 can raise stake sizing beyond what the 0.5-unit cap intends only if cap logic at sportsbook.py:205 is skipped (cap applies only when stake_cap is not None; threshold-only tightening caps at 1 unit via evidence_decisions.py:93). Verify no path leaves adjusted-edge stakes uncapped. (2) evidence_decisions.py:122,144 uses date-string comparison (history date < now.date()) as a temporal-leakage guard; same-day games already completed or timezone mismatches (UTC date vs local game date) could admit or wrongly reject history; also trend rows are only date-checked, not tied to the quote time. Definite-ish gap: the injury 'latest' availability check (line 117-118) requires the absent player's rows to all be 'out', but self.availability is populated only when all rows share one fetched_utc stamp (line 61-62), so a single multi-stamp file silently disables all availability holds without recording an error. (3) sportsbook.py:164-172 settlement and 156-163 references: pregame-reference INSERT OR REPLACE can overwrite a prior reference with a later-observed quote on re-run; since game_quotes is capped at tip-1us this is bounded, but the stored label is unverified. Also belief() (sportsbook.py:104-133) applies a bias then context.game may further change probability (CFB policy at evidence_decisions.py:166 plus saved research note warns against double-adding EPA); the double-adjustment risk between fixed group bias and CFB/EPA evidence is unvalidated. Probability weights WEIGHTS are explicitly unfitted; tests are stale for this snapshot, so rerun before approval.

events.detail: 1) news_hypotheses.py:24-36/62-69 and context_trends.py:63-70: failure handling is fragile. In news_hypotheses.tick, if history_source or injuries load fails, `source`/`meta` are unbound, but the exception path only sets history=None, so later use is guarded only by that flag; however an exception type outside (OSError,ValueError,KeyError) (e.g., pandas ParserError/EmptyDataError, AttributeError on missing columns like fetched_utc/nba_team_id) will crash the whole tick before the transaction. Hypothesis, not definite bug. 2) Temporal/identity concerns: news_hypotheses.py:84/98 identity digest includes source sha256 and history sha256, so every new injury snapshot or history refresh creates a fresh hypothesis for the same game/player/stat, contradicting the comment at line 97 ('one predeclared hypothesis per player/stat/game') and enabling post-hoc cherry-picking and duplicate settled rows inflating Brier/unit stats in public() (lines 139-150). Likely definite design defect. Also line 93-95 compares nba_player_id/nba_team_id strings to pid/team without normalization; a dtype/format mismatch silently yields 'No confirmed-out teammate'. 3) Calibration/model quality: hypothesis() line 54 shrinks the without-teammate mean toward baseline but the baseline already uses last-30 games (which may include the absence), and line 56 scales mean linearly with minutes; edge>=.02 threshold at line 117 is uncalibrated, 'SHADOW_CANDIDATE' unit returns (line 147) are selected on the same quote (best-edge option, line 110) so are optimistically biased; no multiple-comparison control. context_trends line 85 picks min(book) alphabetically rather than best price, and context() lines 26-38 treat a quote observed up to 90 minutes pre-tip as the line (not closing), though it is disclosed. Tests are for a different snapshot, so nothing here is certified.

bankroll_policy: New paper stakes: at most 40% committed overall, 10% per sport, 2% per game and 1% per ticket. At most 10% committed beyond 24 hours. Sportsbook NBA/NFL game lines may use 7.5% per sport, leaving 2.5% of bankroll for props within the 10% sport limit. Percentages use the lower of initial bankroll and current cash plus open stakes; profits do not automatically increase limits. Existing locked tickets remain intact, and may exceed new limits until settlement. Model and sportsbook accounts stay separate.
